es: Verificar una historia viral: evaluar tres afirmaciones, señalar la evidencia que falta y redactar un veredicto matizado.

teaching.en: Before we confirm a viral story, we ask whether it can be traced back to an original source, not just a screenshot.
teaching.es: Antes de confirmar una historia viral, nos preguntamos si puede rastrearse hasta una fuente original y no solo una captura de pantalla.
teaching.explanationEs: Confirm = obtener una prueba independiente; traced back to va con participio pasivo.
segments: Before we confirm a viral story, we ask whether it can
be traced back to an original source, not just a screenshot.

teaching.en: Fact-checkers rate as misleading any genuine photograph that is presented as recent when it was taken years ago.
teaching.es: Los verificadores califican como engañosa cualquier fotografía auténtica que se presente como reciente cuando se tomó hace años.
teaching.explanationEs: Misleading: el dato es real, pero la presentación induce a error.
segments: Fact-checkers rate as misleading any genuine photograph that is
presented as recent when it was taken years ago.

teaching.en: If a claim cannot be confirmed and no evidence appears, it is unproven, and it may not hold up once someone examines it.
teaching.es: Si una afirmación no puede confirmarse y no aparece ninguna prueba, está sin demostrar, y puede que no resista cuando alguien la examine.
teaching.explanationEs: Unproven no es lo mismo que false: falta la prueba, pero nadie ha demostrado lo contrario.
segments: If a claim cannot be confirmed and no evidence appears, it is
unproven, and it may not hold up once someone examines it.
teaching.audioText: If a claim cannot be confirmed and no evidence appears, it is unproven, and it may not hold up once someone examines it.

teaching.en: Our verdict is partly true: the figure is accurate, but the claim about its cause has not been established.
teaching.es: Nuestro veredicto es en parte cierto: la cifra es exacta, pero la afirmación sobre su causa no se ha establecido.
teaching.explanationEs: Un veredicto matizado evalúa cada afirmación por separado.
segments: Our verdict is partly true: the figure is accurate, but
the claim about its cause has not been established.
teaching.audioText: Our verdict is partly true: the figure is accurate, but the claim about its cause has not been established.

teaching.en: It took one reporter ten minutes to debunk the clip, which had been cut and shared out of context.
teaching.es: A un reportero le bastaron diez minutos para desmentir el vídeo, que había sido recortado y compartido fuera de contexto.
teaching.explanationEs: Debunk exige una prueba concreta de que algo es falso o engañoso.

teaching.en: A tentative conclusion, such as the claim is probably false, leaves room for new evidence, whereas a final verdict does not.
teaching.es: Una conclusión provisional, como «la afirmación probablemente es falsa», deja espacio a nuevas pruebas, mientras que un veredicto final no.
teaching.explanationEs: Tentative marca una conclusión abierta a revisión.

prompt.es: ¿Qué veredicto resume un dato real presentado en un contexto falso?

choices.text: Misleading: the photo is real, but its date and place are wrong.
True: the photo shows a real flood, so the claim is correct.
Unproven: nobody has been able to find the original photo.

feedback.es: La imagen es auténtica y procede de una tormenta de hace cinco años; lo que engaña es la fecha que se le atribuye.

hint.es: Busca el veredicto para algo que es real pero mal presentado.

origin.text: A viral photo shows a flooded station with the label Yesterday, in the capital. The picture is genuine, but a news archive shows that it was taken during a storm five years ago.

prompt.es: Completa: «El vídeo es real, pero se compartió fuera de contexto.»

feedback.es: Out of context describe material auténtico al que se le ha quitado lo que explica su sentido.

hint.es: Preposición de la expresión ___ of context.

origin.text: The footage of the festival is real. However, it was cut and shared ___ of context, so viewers got a wrong idea of what happened.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El rumor se rastreó hasta un blog anónimo.»

answer.text: The rumour was traced back to an anonymous blog

feedback.es: Was traced back to forma la pasiva que señala el origen de un rumor.

hint.es: Pasiva: was + participio + back to + origen.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué la verificación califica la afirmación como «partly true»?

choices.text: The rise is real, but the airport is presented as its only cause.
The rise is real, but it happened only in the district beside the airport.
The figures are correct, but they come from an unreliable source.
The airport caused the rise, but the size of it was overstated.

feedback.es: Los precios subieron, pero la verificación recuerda que los expertos atribuyen la mayor parte a la escasez de vivienda: la afirmación presenta una sola causa como toda la historia.

origin.text: The claim that the new airport doubled local rents is partly true. Rents did rise, according to the official figures, but by nine per cent, and experts link most of the rise to a housing shortage. The airport may have contributed, yet the claim presents a single cause as the whole story.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye el locutor sobre el vídeo del río.

choices.text: The footage has been edited, so the whole story is false.
The footage is genuine but belongs to another time and place.
A spill probably happened, but nobody has confirmed it yet.
The river turned red, although for a natural reason.

feedback.es: Las imágenes son reales pero corresponden a un accidente anterior en otro país; por eso la historia es engañosa.

origin.audio: A widely shared video claims that a famous river has turned red because of an oil spill. I searched for the original and found the same footage in a report from three years ago about a mining accident in another country. So the clip is real, but it is being shown out of context. Until someone confirms a recent spill, I would call the story misleading.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada situación con el veredicto que merece.

pairs: The figure is correct, but its cause is unproven.
A real photograph with the wrong date.
No source can be found for the quote.
The official report contradicts the claim.

feedback.es: Cada situación recibe un veredicto distinto: en parte cierto, engañoso, sin demostrar y falso.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el cambio de organismo examinador del colegio.

choices.text: That the exam results were probably invented by the school.
That the ban had no effect on pupils under twelve.
That the rise in results may have another explanation.
That the head teacher hid the change from the parents.

feedback.es: Si el colegio cambió de organismo examinador el mismo año, la mejora podría deberse a eso: por eso la afirmación resulta engañosa, sin que se acuse a nadie de inventar datos.

origin.audio: The story spread quickly: a school in the north had supposedly banned homework, saved millions and raised exam results. We checked three claims. First, the ban: the head teacher confirmed it, but only for pupils under twelve, so the claim is partly true. Second, the saving: no figure has been published, so we rate it as unproven. Third, the rise in results: it is real, yet the school changed its exam board in the same year, which makes the claim misleading. Our tentative conclusion is that the homework ban may have helped, but the evidence does not yet show it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué evidencia falta para sostener que el tranvía salva vidas?

choices.text: Monthly figures confirming that hospital visits for breathing problems have dropped since the tram opened.
A quote from a doctor saying that the tram is good for the town.
Figures on how many passengers the tram carried over the last year.
Evidence that similar towns without a tram saw no similar drop in hospital visits.

feedback.es: Para pasar de la correlación a la causa hace falta descartar otros factores; repetir la caída de las visitas, una opinión o el número de pasajeros no prueba que el tranvía las haya reducido.

origin.text: Our town has the cleanest air in the country, thanks to the new tram. Hospital visits for breathing problems have dropped since it opened, so the tram is clearly saving lives.

prompt.es: Completa: «Calificamos la afirmación de engañosa, no de falsa.»

feedback.es: Rate the claim as + veredicto es la fórmula del verificador; aquí el veredicto es misleading.

origin.text: The photo is genuine, but its label is wrong. For that reason we ___ the claim as misleading rather than false.

prompt.es: Redacta la verificación: tres afirmaciones, evidencia que falta y conclusión provisional.

answer.text: Our check of the viral story gives a mixed picture. First, the video seems genuine, but it has no date and no original source, so it was probably shared out of context, and we rate the claim that it shows a secret payment as unproven. Second, the council says that the envelope was a gift for a school, and nobody has confirmed the blogger's version, which comes from an anonymous source. Third, the official figures confirm that the parks budget fell by twelve per cent, so that claim is true, although the fall is not necessarily linked to the video. What is missing is hard evidence: a dated recording, the receipt for the gift and a statement from the people who were there. Until we see them, our tentative conclusion is that the story is partly true and misleading, because a real figure has been connected to an unproven claim. It is arguably unfair to blame the mayor, and it would be reasonable to wait for more evidence before we share the story.
accepted: Our check of the viral story gives a mixed picture. First, the video seems genuine, but it has no date and no original source, so it was probably shared out of context, and we rate the claim that it shows a secret payment as unproven. Second, the council says that the envelope was a gift for a school, and nobody has confirmed the blogger's version, which comes from an anonymous source. Third, the official figures confirm that the parks budget fell by twelve per cent, so that claim is true, although the fall is not necessarily linked to the video. What is missing is hard evidence: a dated recording, the receipt for the gift and a statement from the people who were there. Until we see them, our tentative conclusion is that the story is partly true and misleading, because a real figure has been connected to an unproven claim. It is arguably unfair to blame the mayor, and it would be reasonable to wait for more evidence before we share the story.

We have checked the three claims in the viral story, and the result is mixed. The video seems genuine, but it carries no date and cannot be traced back to an original source, so we rate the claim that it shows a secret payment as unproven. The blogger is an anonymous source, and nobody has confirmed his account, while the council says that the envelope contained a gift for a school. The official figures do confirm that the parks budget fell by twelve per cent, so this claim is true, although the drop is not necessarily linked to the video. The evidence we still need is simple: a dated recording, a receipt for the gift and a statement from someone who was present. For now, our tentative conclusion is that the story is partly true and misleading, because it connects a real figure to a claim that has not been proved. The mayor may be innocent, and waiting would be the reasonable course.

feedback.es: Una verificación completa evalúa cada afirmación, nombra la evidencia que falta y termina con una conclusión provisional y prudente.

origin.text: Historia viral: un vídeo sin fecha muestra a un alcalde recibiendo un sobre. Un blog anónimo asegura que es un pago secreto y que por eso el presupuesto de parques bajó un 12 %. El municipio dice que era un regalo para una escuela. Las cifras oficiales confirman la bajada del 12 %. Evalúa las tres afirmaciones, indica qué evidencia falta y redacta una conclusión matizada (240–300 palabras).

prompt.es: ¿Por qué prefiere Tom la etiqueta «unverified» a «false»?

choices.text: Because the lack of a source does not prove that the quote is invented.
Because the famous author has already denied writing the quote.
Because two sites repeat the quote, which confirms that it is genuine.
Because unverified is the usual label for any quote attributed to a famous author.

feedback.es: Tom no encuentra fuente, pero eso no demuestra que la cita sea inventada; por eso deja abierta una corrección futura.

origin.text: Dear Mar, the viral quote is attributed to a famous author, but I could not trace it back to any of her books. Two sites repeat it, yet both take it from the same blog, which names no source at all. I would not call it false yet. I would say unverified, and leave room for a correction if someone finds the source. Best wishes, Tom.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tras sopesar las pruebas, los verificadores llegaron a un veredicto prudente.»

feedback.es: Un verdict es la valoración final del verificador; aquí es prudente porque solo una parte de la historia se sostiene.

origin.text: The fact-checkers spent a week on the story. After weighing all the evidence, they reached a cautious ___: partly true.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La afirmación no resiste un examen minucioso.»

answer.text: The claim does not hold up under scrutiny
accepted: The claim does not hold up under scrutiny
Under scrutiny the claim does not hold up

feedback.es: Hold up under scrutiny es la colocación para algo que no sobrevive a un examen detallado.
